assignments.reason: The act of rejoicing in God (שמשמח את עצמו באלקיו) is essentially a devotional orientation toward the divine presence. The word באלקיו ('in his God') directly references the indwelling divine aspect — the Shekhinah. The entire Torah teaches that this rejoicing is the tikkun of the Shekhinah: through it the deficiencies 'from the Shekhinah' are completed. The node's essential nature is inseparable from the Shekhinah — it is the human act whose entire meaning is defined by and directed toward the divine presence that Package 1 represents.

assignments.node_id: נשלמו כל החסרונות מהשבירה, ונתעלה כל הניצוצות. וזה אנכי אשמח בה, יתמו  ונשלמו כל החטאים
assignments.reason: This composite node describes the restored wholeness of the Shekhinah. The deficiencies (חסרונות) are explicitly 'from the Shekhinah' (נחסרו מהשכינה) — they are her lacks. The sparks (ניצוצות) that fell in the Breaking fell from her. The verse 'יתמו חטאים מן הארץ' is interpreted as 'deficiencies are completed from the Upper Earth = the Shekhinah.' The node's essential nature is the state of the Shekhinah made whole — the fulfilled, complete divine presence. It belongs to the Shekhinah package by its very definition.
